newsitem.title: FINLAND: WEEK AHEAD - FINNISH MARKETS STAY ON U.S. DATA WATCH.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - FINNISH MARKETS STAY ON U.S. DATA WATCH.

text.p: Finnish financial markets will continue to monitor U.S. economic indicators next week, and domestic figures could have an impact only if they were way off forecasts, analysts said.

Early next week, investors are expected to monitor the aftermath of Friday's U.S. employment data -- an unexpectedly big rise in December non-farm payrolls, which caused U.S. treasuries to weaken sharply and the Dow Jones to open lower.
On Tuesday, U.S. December CPI and industrial production figures are due. At home, December CPI and November industrial production come on Wednesday and PPI on Friday.
U.S. AND GERMAN FIGURES SEEN KEY

"Inflation fears (in the U.S.) are expected to pick up and pressures for higher interest rates will mount if economic indicators show strong growth," said Jukka Huuskonen, chief analyst at Arctos Securities.
If interest rates rose, U.S. stocks prices would fall, pushing Finnish shares weaker, too, analysts said.

U.S. December CPI will be released on Tuesday at 1530/1330 GMT. In November, it rose 0.3 percent month-on-month and 3.3 percent year-on-year. December capacity utilisation and industrial production date are due at 1615/1415 GMT.
Esko Torsti chief economist at SE-Banken in Helsinki, said that even though the U.S. figures are important guidelines for the Finnish markets, investors should also focus on the German economy.
"The German economy is weak and it is unsure whether Germany can fulfil the budget deficit criterion (for EMU)," he said, adding that this could pose a threat to the entire EMU process.
The German bond market could then firm at the expense of peripheral countries like Finland, Torsti said.
FINNISH ECONOMIC INDICATORS UNLIKELY TO SURPRISE
On Wednesday, December CPI is due at 0700/0500 GMT. The mean forecast by five economists for the year-on-year CPI rise is 0.8 percent, up from 0.7 percent in November.
November industrial production figures will be released on Wednesday at 0700/0500 GMT as well. Economists' mean forecast is for a year-on-year rise of 6.1 percent after a 6.8 percent rise in October.
"If industrial output turns out to be weaker than forecast it may dent Q4 GDP growth expectations," said Postipankki chief economist Tarja Heinonen said.
Finnish stocks could suffer from weaker-than-expected industrial production data, she added.

December construction costs are due for release on Tuesday at 0700/0500 GMT. In November, costs fell by 0.4 percent year-on-year. On Friday, December PPI, wholesale prices and export and import prices are scheduled for release at 0700/0500 GMT.
In November, Finnish PPI fell 1.8 percent year-on-year.
GOOD DEMAND SEEN FOR T-BILL ON TUESDAY
The State Treasury Office (STO) will issue T-bills in maturities of 89, 180 and 364 days in its weekly auction on Tuesday.
SE-Banken's Torsti expected good demand. Corporations seem to have plenty of liquidity at the moment and T-bills are considered attractive after the recent fall in bond yields, he said.
--Tuula Franck, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 245
